cases.purpose: Two groups in the scan, the echo's the strongest; anchoring off keeps the echo, anchoring on moves the burst to the direct path's group.

channel.model: two-path Watterson (Rayleigh) channel, PathSim rev-6; Table XX of MIL-STD-188-110B (JITC 2004 Table 10.1) row 300 bps, 5 ms, 5 Hz, 7 dB
channel.paths_note: equal average power: PathSim scales each path by 1/sqrt(number of paths). The second path's delay is exactly 8 samples/ms at 8 kHz, so it is 240 (5 ms) or 96 (2 ms) samples at 48 kHz; measured 240.00003 and 96.00002 (calibration P5-CAL-DELAY-v1).

doppler.meaning: PathSim's spread is the 2-sigma bandwidth of the Gaussian-shaped low-pass filter that shapes each path's complex Gaussian tap process (the Table value is the 2-sigma width), applied to both paths

seed.generator: the C runtime's rand(), srand(seed): one stream drives both paths' Rayleigh generators and the noise, in an order that does not depend on the signal; the fading is advanced 4.0 s (discarded) before the first sample

snr.definition: signal power over noise power in a 300-3300 Hz band, over the span of the transmit audio (unpadded burst), measured from PathSim's own truth export on a non-fading render of the same input
snr.offset_reason: PathSim holds the noise at a constant absolute level and sets the signal gain from a block-wise running RMS of its input; the silent lead pulls that average down, so the signal is about 0.9 dB too strong at the start of the burst and the span-average SNR is higher than commanded. The base offset -0.40 dB (burst alone: span SNR 7.03 dB at target 7.0) is lowered per mode so the span with lead and tail meets the target
snr.note: a target, not a measured SNR of this recording: the recording's fading makes its instantaneous SNR vary around the calibrated average

timeline.calibration_method: chain delay: the transmit audio through the identical chain with one non-fading path at 0 ms (PathSim --spread 0) and no noise, lead and tail present; cross-correlation peak (parabolic and exact DTFT) and cross-spectrum phase slope over 400-3200 Hz agree to 1e-4 sample (174.0000; PathSim's symmetric Hilbert filter delays 29 samples at 8 kHz, the resamplers none). tx_symbol0_center_offset_samples is from the transmitter's shaping code (BodyAudioStreamModulator::render_window: symbol s reaches output sample n through tap n + 320 - 20 s, the pulse peak, so symbol 0 is centred on transmit sample 0). Second path: two static paths, transfer-function phase, 240.00003 and 96.00002 samples. The receiver is a cross-check only.
operations: transmit audio generated (unpadded, 24-bit)
24000 zeros added before and 24000 after at 48 kHz (PCM24), before any channel stage
level stage -12 dB and resampling 48 kHz -> 8 kHz (PCM16)
PathSim, seeded; fading advanced 4.0 s and discarded before the first sample; no output samples discarded
resampling 8 kHz -> 48 kHz (PCM16)
no trimming, no normalization; output frames = input frames
